check.leadText:
CITIES UNDER GALE RISK
Manila
Pasay City
TIME TO PREPARE
Signal No. 2 level (Tropical Storm, 62–88 km/h)
24 hours

The strongest forecast wind is 74.0 km/h in Manila. PAGASA usually raises a Signal No. 2 about 24 hours before winds of this strength arrive.

Pasay City: 36 hours (Signal No. 1 reference). Forecast date: Thursday, October 15, 2026. This daily forecast does not specify an exact wind-arrival hour.

24 and 36 hours are reference warning lead times, not countdowns. Follow the official PAGASA bulletin for the actual signal and timing.

WHAT YOU SHOULD DO
Stay indoors and away from windows during peak wind hours.
Secure or bring inside all loose outdoor items: chairs, pots, signs, and hanging objects.
Avoid unnecessary travel, especially on motorcycles and bicycles.
Check on elderly neighbors and those living in informal or vulnerable housing.
Keep the emergency hotlines below ready. Tap a number to call.
Monitor official PAGASA advisories and local government announcements for updates.
IMPACTS ON PEOPLE & COMMUNITIES
Risk of injury from flying debris and unsecured outdoor objects at gale-force speeds.
Extremely difficult and dangerous to walk outdoors, as strong gusts can knock pedestrians off balance.
Motorcyclists and cyclists face severe side-wind hazard; travel is strongly discouraged.
Potential structural damage to poorly constructed buildings, fences, roofing, and signage.
Tree branches may snap; risk of falling limbs onto roads, walkways, and parked vehicles.
Risk of power line disruption and loss of communication infrastructure in affected areas.
EMERGENCY HOTLINES
Emergency

911
